A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have synthesized a charge transfer amplified fluorescent sensor 3 for the detection of Hg(2+), which shows a turn-on response with a detection limit of 0.1 mu M, and the in-situ prepared 3-HG(2+) complex was used for detection of PA via electrostatic interaction.
a new chemosensor has been developed which is able to detect picric acid and to perform logic functions.

a new fluorescent chemosensor has been designed and synthesized for Hg2+, which can detect Hg2+ with high sensitivity, and the chemosensor 1 can detect picric acid via the electrostatic interaction between the picric acid and the in situ generated 1-Hg2+ complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple fluorescent probe, 3, which can be synthesized in a few minutes from readily available materials, is sufficient to construct a complex logic circuit.
the fluorescence of 3-Hg2+ can be switched on and off in response to picric acid and 2,2'-bipyridyl (bpy) via electrostatic interaction, which can be utilized to design logic circuits.
the 3-Hg2+ complex can be used as a fluorescent probe for picric acid and for construction of logic gates.
